newsitem.title: USA: U.S. low-cost carriers form trade association.
newsitem.headline: U.S. low-cost carriers form trade association.

text.p: A group of U.S. low-cost airlines on Wednesday announced the formation of an association that would ask the federal government to address what its members view as anti-competitive practices by the major carriers.

At a media conference in Washington monitored in Denver, officials of the new group, known as the Air Carrier Association of America, said they would meet with members of Congress involved in transportation issues.
The members of the association are Airtran Corp, Frontier Airlines Inc, Kiwi International Air Lines, Laker Airways Inc, Reno Air Inc, Spirit Airlines, Sun Jet international and Valujet Inc.
The group plans to ask the Department of Transportation (DOT) to take steps to help low-cost carriers operate competitive schedules at high-density airports.
It also wants the DOT to establish clear guidelines for identifying pricing, scheduling and other practices the group considers to be anti-competitive.
Frontier Airlines has already contacted federal authorities about what it says are predatory practices by UAL Corp's United Airlines. United has denied the allegation.
